facts: $\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\le \mathrm{Var}(f)\le \mathrm{I}(f)$: the first because $\mathrm{Inf}_i = \sum_{S\ni i}\hat f(S)^2$ is part of the sum defining $\mathrm{Var}$, the second because $|S|\ge 1$ off the empty set.
Every non-constant $f$ has $\mathrm{Var}(f)\ge 2^{2-n}(1-2^{-n})$, attained by $\mathrm{OR}_n$ and $\mathrm{AND}_n$.
$\mathrm{Var}$ is not monotone under restriction and does not compose: $\mathrm{Var}(f\circ g)$ depends on the bias of $g$, which is exactly why biased gadgets destroy Fourier lower bounds.
self.name: Variance
self.short: How far f is from constant. Not a complexity measure -- the unit the other Fourier quantities are divided by.
